title: Continue a journal investigation from an exact cursor
goal: Retain a boot identity and opaque journal cursor, then isolate only later practice events without changing journal retention.
challenge: Record a unique tag and current boot ID. Emit and retain a first marker/cursor, emit a later marker, and prove the after-cursor query excludes the first. Retain invalid-cursor failure and inspect disk use/boots read-only. Explain persistence, Resume and the limits of retained evidence.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/operations-journalcursor.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && saved_umask=$(umask) && umask 077 && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/operations-journalcursor.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; dir_ok() { test -d "$1" && test ! -L "$1" && test "$(realpath -e -- "$1")" = "$w/$1"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here && test "$(df --output=avail -k . | tail -1)" -gt 65536
steps.explanation: Create and record a new private guest workspace. Stop on any failed guard; the free-space check is an observation, not a guaranteed reserve. Do not use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A unique learner-owned mode0700 directory; no originals overwritten.

steps.command: here && fresh boot.txt first.txt cursor.txt later.txt rejected.txt storage.txt && tag=ll-cursor-${w##*.} && tr -d '-' < /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id > boot.txt && logger -t "$tag" FIRST && sudo journalctl --sync && sudo journalctl -b "$(cat boot.txt)" -t "$tag" --no-pager -n 1 -o cat --show-cursor > first.txt && sed -n 's/^-- cursor: //p' first.txt > cursor.txt && test "$(wc -l < cursor.txt)" = 1 && grep -qx FIRST first.txt && cat first.txt
steps.explanation: journalctl -b requires the 32-character boot ID: remove only the kernel UUID’s hyphens. The cursor is an opaque position, not a timestamp or guarantee of indefinite retention. Pin the explicit boot ID rather than assuming -1 is the desired boot.
steps.expected: FIRST and one journal cursor; exact boot ID retained.

steps.command: here && fresh later.txt && logger -t "$tag" SECOND && sudo journalctl --sync && sudo journalctl -b "$(cat boot.txt)" -t "$tag" --after-cursor="$(cat cursor.txt)" --no-pager -o cat > later.txt && grep -qx SECOND later.txt && ! grep -qx FIRST later.txt && cat later.txt
steps.explanation: Quote the entire cursor. Cursor continuation selects later matching entries; no record deletion or journal configuration change.
steps.expected: Only SECOND in the later practice query.

steps.command: here && fresh rejected.txt storage.txt && { sudo journalctl --after-cursor=NOT_A_CURSOR --no-pager > rejected.txt 2>&1; rc=$?; test "$rc" != 0; } && sudo journalctl --disk-usage > storage.txt && sudo journalctl --list-boots --no-pager >> storage.txt && cat storage.txt
steps.explanation: Disk use and boot availability are observations, not a promised retention period. Invalid cursors fail; do not silently switch to a broader query.
steps.expected: Invalid cursor retained as failure; current storage/boot list read-only.

hints: Use a saved exact boot ID and quote the opaque cursor.
Missing old entries are not proof an event never happened.
review: I retained actual statuses, bytes and relevant identities, including the incorrect case; successful command exit alone is not my evidence.
I can explain the stated limitations and independently meet the Challenge outcomes. Completion records my self-review, not an automatic assessment.
I preserved originals and inspected the exact cleanup inventory before deleting only this recorded practice workspace.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 partial 108.2 journal cursor/boot/persistence. Self-reviewed and unscored; no complete-objective, exam-readiness or LPI-endorsement claim.
